extracted.intended_audience: H-1B petitioners and employers, immigration attorneys and representatives, USCIS/DHS program implementers, and public commenters on H-1B rulemakings
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements, procedural standards, and analytical methods for implementing a wage‑level weighted H-1B registration and petition process, including required data elements on registration/petition forms, selection weighting, data handling rules for the regulatory impact analysis, and boundaries of regulatory analyses. Targeted at parties who register or petition for H-1B beneficiaries and those evaluating the rule’s impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion of reported pay frequencies to annual amounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Average annual salary estimates for H-1B cap-subject workers were derived from LCA wage data by converting all reported pay frequencies to annual amounts using standard factors (hourly × 2,080; weekly × 52; monthly × 12; annual as reported) and then computing the mean.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the stated standard conversion factors for hourly, weekly, and monthly pay before computing means; document conversions and assumptions so estimates in tables (e.g., Table 15) can be replicated without releasing individual-level raw data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Top-coding of extreme high annualized wages
rubrics_metrics.description: To mitigate undue influence from extreme high values and apparent entry errors, annualized wages were top coded at $1,000,000.99 (recoded to one million in practice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Top-code extreme high values to limit influence on means while preserving the original distribution shape; explicitly state top-code threshold in analysis. The lower tail was reviewed and no anomalies found, so no bottom-coding was applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review for anomalies and bottom-coding policy
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS conducted a review of the lower tail of wage data and identified no anomalies; therefore no bottom-coding or exclusions were applied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform lower-tail review for implausible low values; only apply bottom-coding or exclusions if anomalies are documented. Document quality checks and findings to justify not excluding low values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality checks for internal consistency of salary estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS conducted quality checks to ensure internal consistency in the average annual salary for H-1B cap-subject workers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement and document quality-control procedures (e.g., internal consistency checks) on processed wage data used in regulatory impact tables so reviewers can assess the reliability of aggregated estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weighted selection based on OEWS wage level
rubrics_metrics.description: USCIS will weight and select each unique beneficiary (or petition, if registration is suspended) such that a beneficiary assigned to OEWS wage level IV is entered four times into the selection pool; level III entered three times; level II two times; and level I once.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the specified multiplicative weights exactly (4,3,2,1) based on assigned OEWS wage level when constructing the selection pool; ensure the underlying rule that selection remains random but weighted is preserved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registrant must select highest OEWS wage level equal to or below proffered wage
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant will be required to select the box for the highest OEWS wage level that the beneficiary’s wage generally equals or exceeds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On the electronic registration form, registrants must identify the highest wage level met by the proffered wage; this selection determines the weight applied in the selection pool and must reflect the wage as of the registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required data elements on registration: SOC code and area of intended employment
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants must provide the SOC code for the proffered position and the area of intended employment that served as the basis for the OEWS wage level indicated on the registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure SOC code and geographic area are provided on registration; these elements are used to determine the correct OEWS wage level and to detect inconsistencies or gaming.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition must include evidence of basis for wage level selected on registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitioners will be required to submit evidence of the basis of the wage level selected on the registration as of the date that the registration underlying the petition was submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When filing the H-1B petition after selection, include documentary evidence supporting the wage-level choice recorded at registration (e.g., pay offer records, LCA details) to allow USCIS to verify the registration selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition must match registration and LCA identifying/position information
rubrics_metrics.description: An H-1B petition filed after registration selection must contain and be supported by the same identifying information and position information—including OEWS wage level, SOC code, and area of intended employment—provided in the selected registration and indicated on the LCA used to support the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure consistency across registration, LCA, and petition; discrepancies may prompt USCIS scrutiny and enforcement actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: USCIS enforcement for attempts to game selection
rubrics_metrics.description: USCIS may deny a subsequent new or amended petition or revoke an approved petition if USCIS determines that the filing of the new or amended petition was part of the petitioner’s attempt to unfairly increase odds of selection during the registration (or petition, if applicable) selection process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid filing strategies intended to alter selection probabilities after registration; retain records demonstrating bona fide job offers and legitimate reasons for any post-registration changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form I-129 supplement questions (7–11) required and placed in section 1
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions 7 through 11 on the H-1B and H-1B1 Data Collection and Filing Fee Exemption Supplement (e.g., education level required, SOC, wage level) are directly related to and necessary for implementing this rule and will remain in section 1 of the supplement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include these items in the general information section of the supplement; DHS considers them self-explanatory and derived from DOL prevailing wage guidance, so separate instructional text is not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow DOL prevailing wage/PWD guidance when OEWS data unavailable
rubrics_metrics.description: In the limited instance where there is no current OEWS prevailing wage information for the proffered position, the registrant would follow DOL guidance on Prevailing Wage Determinations (PWDs) to determine which OEWS wage level to select on the registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the most current DOL PWD guidance (as published) to determine wage level when OEWS data are absent; DHS notes that registrants should use any updated DOL guidance in effect at the time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of Paperwork Reduction Act (PRA) analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: The PRA analysis is limited to burdens associated with the information collection (forms and registration tool); the PRA requires agencies to minimize paperwork burdens but does not require addressing costs outside the information collection requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing PRA analyses, quantify and justify burden hours and costs tied specifically to the information collection instrument(s); broader economic harms or programmatic costs fall outside PRA burden accounting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden estimates should cover all H-1B petitions when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS estimated the burden of the additional registration/petition questions for all H-1B petitions, not just cap-subject petitions, because these requirements would apply to any H-1B petitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare burden estimates using the full universe of affected filings when the form changes apply beyond the subset (e.g., cap-subject) that prompted the rule, and explain the population considered in burden calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: RIA methodology: use observed data for tenure assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rule updated the average tenure assumption from 4 years (NPRM) to a 5-year average based on observed extensions; this longer average increases the 10-year totals for benefits and transfers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Base multi-year accrual or duration assumptions on observed administrative data where available; document changes from proposed to final assumptions and quantify effects on long-term benefit/transfer estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: RIA accounting conventions and discounting per OMB Circular A-4
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS presents annualized and discounted impacts at both 3% and 7% discount rates and follows OMB Circular A-4 accounting statement conventions when reporting costs, benefits, and transfers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report RIA results under standard OMB conventions (3% and 7% discount rates, annualized monetized benefits/costs/transfers, qualitative unquantified items) and cite applicable OMB guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of selection population and beneficiary-centric random selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the final rule, USCIS will continue to monitor unique-beneficiary registrations during the announced registration period and perform random selection among unique beneficiaries (or petitions if registration is suspended), with the addition that entries are weighted by wage level as specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain beneficiary-centric uniqueness rules (one registration per unique beneficiary counts) and apply random selection across that universe, incorporating the wage-level multiplicative weights; document whether selection is of beneficiaries or petitions when registration is suspended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of out-of-scope comments
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS will not provide substantive responses to comments outside the scope of this rulemaking (e.g., calls to terminate the H-1B program, changes to statutory cap, comments requiring DOL action, comments about other visa categories).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When submitting comments, focus on issues within the rule’s specified scope (administration of H-1B numerical allocations and the registration/selection process); expect out-of-scope topics to receive only a brief overview rather than substantive response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting of costs, benefits, and transfers by provision
rubrics_metrics.description: Table 1.3 and related tables summarize each final-rule provision’s description, estimated quantitative costs (e.g., petitioners' $15M registration/petition burden), qualitative effects, and transfers (e.g., estimated $858M transfer in FY2026), with narrative linking provisions to estimated impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When documenting regulatory impacts, provide a provision-by-provision table linking rule elements to quantified and unquantified costs, benefits, and transfers; explicitly note which impacts are transfers vs. net benefits.
